title: もう後戻りできないぞ  (No Turning Back Now)

segments.t: Walking through Susukino at night, the protagonist spots magazines sealed in clear plastic wrap so browsers cannot peek inside without buying. When his new partner tells him they sell over a million copies every month, he drops all hesitation and marches straight toward a shop called Showtime. Listen to the finale of Episode One.
これは何だ？
ビニールに包まれた中身が見えない本だ。
中身を隠して買わせる新しい本なんだよ。
これを考えた人は頭が切れるよな。
これ、月にどのぐらい売れてるんだ？
月に百万冊以上は売れてるらしい。
百万冊！？
トシ、これを仕入れることはできるか？
急に呼び捨てかよ。
まあ、あのショータイムだ。もう後戻りできないぞ。
分かってる。
行ってくる。
Episode One ends with big numbers, sudden familiarity, and the same two-word doorway phrase our protagonist used at home—now with a brand-new meaning.
ビニールに包まれた中身が見えない本だ。
'It is a book wrapped in vinyl so you cannot see the contents.'  It features
中身
joins the word for inside with the word for body or substance—meaning the contents inside a package, bag, or book.
見えない
this word means cannot be seen.
中身を隠して買わせる新しい本なんだよ。
"'It hides what is inside to make people buy it—a new kind of book.' Turning the verb to buy into " The phrase contains
買わせる
expresses making or tempting customers to buy, followed by
新しい
, new.
これを考えた人は頭が切れるよな。
"'Whoever thought this up is really sharp.' Just like English 'sharp', " Pay attention to
頭が切れる
literally says 'the head cuts cleanly'—praising a clever, quick-witted business mind!
これ、月にどのぐらい売れてるんだ？
"'Roughly how many of these sell per month?' Built from the word for which, plus the word for about, " The speaker uses
どのぐらい
asks 'roughly how much?', handy for prices, distances, and sales totals alike.
月に百万冊以上は売れてるらしい。
"'Over a million copies a month, apparently.' Bound books and magazines count with the counter for books. Since the word for ten thousand is used, one hundred ten-thousands—" In this line,
百万
—equals one million, and
らしい
adds 'so I hear'.
トシ、これを仕入れることはできるか？
"'Toshi, can we stock these?' Store owners use " The speaker uses
仕入れる
for buying stock to resell, paired with
ことはできるか
, 'is it possible to?'
急に呼び捨てかよ。
"He says 'Suddenly calling me by my bare first name, huh?' Big cultural moment: " The word
呼び捨て
this word means dropping polite suffixes and calling someone by their bare name alone—showing he just shifted into boss-and-partner mode
急に
, all of a sudden!
もう後戻りできないぞ。
'There is no turning back anymore.'  You can catch
後戻り
combines the word for back with the word for returning—so
もう後戻りできない
warns 'you cannot turn back now'.
分かってる。
"'I know.' Calm, unhurried " Pay attention to
分かってる
drops yesterday's defensive ending—now he means business.
行ってくる。
"'I am going in.' Earlier he used " Watch for
行ってくる

with his kids at the front door; here, and this word is built from the verb to go and the verb to come back, those same words launch a whole new life. Now let's listen to the final scene of Episode One from beginning to end.
これは何だ？
ビニールに包まれた中身が見えない本だ。
中身を隠して買わせる新しい本なんだよ。
これを考えた人は頭が切れるよな。
これ、月にどのぐらい売れてるんだ？
月に百万冊以上は売れてるらしい。
百万冊！？
トシ、これを仕入れることはできるか？
急に呼び捨てかよ。
まあ、あのショータイムだ。もう後戻りできないぞ。
分かってる。
行ってくる。

Congratulations on finishing all of Episode One! You learned the word for contents, the phrase for a sharp mind, the term for dropping polite titles, and saw the everyday doorway phrase come full circle. Until Episode Two—see you next time!
また会いましょう。
